talk_track: Daniel Kirichanski here — my work is standing up engineering leadership inside post-acquisition SaaS companies, the same integration playbook I ran at PayPal after the CyActive deal and again at Tricentis. AddSearch's live Greenhouse posting for a hands-on CTO says the company is 'at an inflection point: maintaining a stable, high-SLA enterprise product while scaling a newer AI/RAG solution.' Read plainly, that means the RAG product is winning deals faster than the platform underneath can absorb, with no technical owner holding both sides. Player-coach CTO searches for 15-person companies tend to run long, because anyone who can carry an enterprise SLA and an AI roadmap is usually already a CTO somewhere. The interim months are where the risk lives: the SLA erodes quietly, or the RAG roadmap ships without an evaluation harness — the failure mode I keep writing about. What breaks first if the search runs long — the SLA or the roadmap?
